# Power bank for flying

The best choice is any power bank under **100 Wh**. That's the FAA limit, and it covers nearly every bank people use ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)). The one product in my search results that fits is the **Baseus Blade H1**.

## My pick: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)
- **Airline-legal:** about 74 Wh, well under the 100 Wh cap.
- **Laptop-capable:** 100 W USB-C output, so it can charge a MacBook Pro as well as your phone. It has 2× USB-C and 2× USB-A ports, and a 100 W cable is included.
- **Flat shape:** 134 × 134 × 18 mm, about 451 g, so it slips into a personal item.
- **Price:** $89.99 (list $99.99), verified Oct 21, 2026, with a 24-month warranty.

**Buy:** [Baseus Blade H1 at Baseus's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). This is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays a commission at no cost to you. Details are on the [product page](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). Prices change, so confirm at checkout.

**Limits of this pick:** My search turned up only this one product, so I haven't compared it against other brands. If you only need to charge a phone, a smaller and cheaper bank would also work. Baseus doesn't publish per-port wattage when several devices charge at once.

## Rules for any power bank
- **Carry-on only.** Power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the bank out and keep it with you ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/prepare_fly/baggage)).
- **Under 100 Wh.** With airline approval you can carry up to two larger banks (101-160 Wh). Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep the bank in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case so the terminals can't short-circuit.
- **Airlines can be stricter.** Southwest now limits each customer to **one** power bank (effective April 20, 2026). It must be under 100 Wh, kept out of the overhead bin, visible while in use, and not charged from in-seat power ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)).
- **Tell the crew** right away if a battery gets hot, swells, or smokes ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).

Check your airline's policy before you fly, since quantity limits and in-flight use rules vary.
